issues.description: Regex name HAS_TIME conflates 'looks like it could contain a time token' with 'has a time'
issues.detail: The pattern /\dm?s/i is a cheap prefilter, not a predicate of 'has time'. It will match strings like '1s' inside identifiers, urls, or content() values. The name complects 'fast reject heuristic' with 'time present'. Rename to LIKELY_HAS_TIME or PREFILTER_TIME so the value semantics are honest about what it asserts.

issues.description: Prefilter is correctness-coupled to valueParser without an explicit invariant
issues.detail: The optimization assumes: if valueParser would find a time node, the raw string contains \dm?s. That is true today but is an implicit contract between a regex and a parser living in separate concerns. Make the relationship explicit with a one-line comment stating the invariant, so a future parser change does not silently start skipping declarations.

issues.description: Property-name lowercasing moved purely for perf, not for clarity
issues.detail: Reordering the unprefixed/lowercase call after the prefilter is fine, but it entangles two unrelated changes (perf gate plus statement reorder) in one diff. Simple would be: compute the prefilter, return, then leave the rest untouched. The current shape is easy to review but slightly complects 'skip early' with 'reshape the function body'.

review.summary: This is a small, mostly SIMPLE change: a cheap regex prefilter short-circuits the expensive valueParser call when no time-like token is present. The values and time semantics are unchanged; only a fast-reject path is added at the edge. The main critique is naming and an implicit contract: HAS_TIME overstates what the regex proves, and the prefilter is silently coupled to valueParser's notion of a time node. INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY is minor and acceptable; the question that should have been asked first is whether walkDecls itself should be filtered by declared time-valued properties, which would be the more decomposed fix.
